item.title: Jermaine Dupri Sues Sony Music for $18M in Unpaid Royalties on Mariah Carey & Usher Albums
item.description:
[Upbeat music fades out, and the host introduces the topic]
Host: "Welcome back to Trending on Billboard. Today, we're talking about a lawsuit that's making waves in the music industry. Legendary hip-hop producer Jermaine Dupri is taking on Sony Music Entertainment, claiming they owe him and his label, So-So Def Recordings, over $18 million in unpaid royalties. Let's dive in."
[Short music transition]
Host: "According to the lawsuit filed on Tuesday, Dupri's label had a 32-year relationship with Sony, but the music giant's accounting practices have been, quote, 'contemptuous' and have harmed So-So Def. The lawsuit claims that royalties for music by Mariah Carey, Usher, Kris Kross, and many others have been understated, and in some cases, not paid at all."
[Short music transition]
Host: "Some notable examples include Kris Kross's hit song 'Jump', which Dupri wrote and produced. He claims Sony never reported producer royalties for their first two albums, including 'Totally Krossed Out', and he's owed over $2 million as a result. The lawsuit also accuses Sony of improperly using bookkeeping tricks to avoid paying royalties, such as claiming that the girl group Xscape still owes over $1.5 million in unrecouped advances, decades after their albums were released."
[Short music transition]
Host: "Dupri's lawyers are calling out Sony's actions as 'unfathomable' and claim that the company tried to hide their actions by using separate accounting systems and amending royalty statements. The lawsuit is seeking payment for the unpaid royalties, and it's a case that could have significant implications for the music industry. We'll be keeping an eye on this story as it develops."
[Outro music starts playing]
Host: "That's all for today's episode of Trending on Billboard. Thanks for tuning in, and we'll catch you on the next one!"
